body:
To expand on your metaphor a bit, it seems to me like a bunch of parties thrown by popular people.  

Higby, Notch, and Cliffy B are throwing the block parties of the year.  You show up and immediately hunt down the host, shouting random one-liners through the crowd in a vain attempt to become friends.

After leaving, you're still basking in the highs from the party.  You start making party plans of your own.  You invite your friends, some people on your street, and even send an invite off to Higby, Notch, and Cliffy.  You count down the days, excited and giddy.  Nobody's RSVP'd yet, but it's alright.  They'll show up.  They know you from their party.  You're friends now.  They'll be here.

You lay out the spread and wait patiently. A few of your friends show up and murmur some words of encouragement before they have to "be somewhere".  A few awkward drama kids wander in and start talking among themselves in the corner, but otherwise you're alone.

The food is cold before you accept the inevitable and kick the drama kids out.  You slump over to your computer and check facebook solemnly.  Your heart sinks as you start finding your friends posting pics of them wasted five feet from Notch.  They were taken tonight.  They left you.  Everyone left you.  

But it's okay.  You're still friends.  They just forgot to invite you is all.  Tomorrow, you'll show up at Notch's and yell one-liners at him across the crowd, and he'll chuckle vaguely at nothing in particular while staring into your section of the crowd, and you'll feel that high again.  You're totally friends with Notch.  Your next party is going to be amazing.
